title: Restoring one customer from backup
summary: Bring back one customer's deleted data without rewinding everyone else.
context: Sampige Clinics' software holds records for 60 centres in one shared PostgreSQL database of 900 GB. Last week a centre's admin deleted a year of appointments by mistake. The only way back was restoring the whole database elsewhere and copying rows by hand, which took two days.
Regulators require records be recoverable, and the team has never actually timed a full restore. Attachments such as scans live in object storage, separately from the database.
must_handle: One centre can be restored to a chosen time, leaving the others untouched.
The restored rows do not clash with what the centre has created since.
Database rows and their attachments come back consistent with each other.
A restore is rehearsed regularly and its time is known.
A backup cannot be deleted by the same mistake or attacker that deleted the data.
show_in_answer: How backups are taken and where they are kept.
The steps of a one-centre restore.
How rows created after the deletion are treated.
How you prove that restores work, and how long they take.
